This petition again coming on for orders upon perusing the  petition and the affidavit filed in support of WP(C) and this Court's  WP(C) No.22681/2013 2/6  order dated 18.02.2025 and upon hearing the arguments of M/S.M.D.JOSEPH,

GOVERNMENT PLEADER for the respondents 1 to 3, SRI.ANEESH JOSEPH, Advocate  for the 4th respondent, DEPUTY SOLICITOR GENERAL OF INDIA &
 SHRI.P.VIJAYAKUMAR, ADDITIONAL SOLICITOR GENERAL OF INDIA for the 6th  respondent and of M/S.M.GOPIKRISHNAN NAMBIAR, K.JOHN MATHAI, JOSON  MANAVALAN, KURYAN THOMAS & PAULOSE C. ABRAHAM, Advocates for the 9th  respondent, the court passed the following:
 WP(C) No.22681/2013 3/6  P.M. MANOJ, J  -----------------------------------
 W.P.(C) Nos.22681, 28121 and 29857 of 2013  &
 3781 and 9482 of 2014  ----------------------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 4th day of March, 2025  ORDER

The petitioner herein is the National Commodity & Derivatives Exchange Limited, which provides an electronic platform for trading in forward contracts in various commodities to all such members who were registered with the petitioner in accordance with its Rules, Bye Laws and Regulations.

On an information from the Food Safety Authorities that the pepper stored in the warehouses were adulterated with Mineral Oil, the 1 st respondent seized over 6800 MT of pepper and decided to take samples and send the same for testing.

The presence of Mineral Oil in black pepper is prohibited as per Regulation 2.9.15 of the Food Safety Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives)
Regulations, 2011.

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, the petitioner approached this Court.
2. In the initial order dated 11.09.2013 and connected orders, the destruction of the commodity as per Clause (2) of Ext.P7 is stayed by this Court for a period of two months.

Thereafter by order dated 28.08.2014, a direction was issued to the 1st respondent to allow the petitioner for cleaning all the sealed WP(C) No.22681/2013 and con.cases stocks of pepper and forward the samples of cleaned pepper to any of the FSSAI notified laboratories.
The modalities for taking out the quantity and the manner in which it has to be taken for testing shall be done by the petitioner as per the direction of the 1st respondent.

3. Thereafter, a further order was passed on 20.02.2015, wherein a direction was issued to the 1 st respondent/Commissioner of Food Safety to cause necessary steps to take samples from the original lot remaining at the hands of the 2nd respondent and send it to the Laboratory at Kolkata for analysis and report.
The outcome was to be made known to this Court as expeditiously as possible.

sentences.text: Later by order dated 12.05.2015, this Court further directed that "the pepper after testing by the notified laboratory found free from impurities and contamination and if that be so there shall be direction to competent among the respondents to release such quantity of the pepper found free from contamination of impurity to the petitioner."

4. By order dated 17.09.2015, while considering this matter again, it is clarified that from the lots, if the result received point out the absence of mineral oil, they shall be released to the petitioner upon satisfaction of compliance with other prescribed food standards, within a period of two months.
WP(C) No.22681/2013 and con.cases 5

. Thereafter, when the matter was considered on 18.02.2025, a direction was given by this Court to the Assistant Commissioner of Food Safety to report to this Court the remaining quantity of black pepper.
Accordingly, it is reported that out of the confiscated 6000 MT of pepper, what remains is 597 MT in NCML warehouse and 405 MT in JICS warehouse.
It is also intimated that in order to release the quantity from these warehouses, both chemical and microbiological analysis has to be done.
For microbiological sampling they already sent a letter to the Commissioner of Food Safety for getting the service of microbiologist from Regional Analytical Lab, Kakkanad.
Whereas some practical difficulties are pointed out.
6. However, that should not stand in the way of taking a decision with respect to releasing unadulterated pepper in stock as aforementioned.
Since it appears that the product was of a crop from 2013, and remained in the custody of the 1 st respondent since then, that may lead to perishing of the crops.
Considering that issue I direct the 1 st respondent to take necessary steps to release the balance products free of impurities within a period of one month.

Sd/-
P.M.MANOJ JUDGE sss 04-03-2025
